title: dedicated gpu pool scheduling/autoscale warmup - debugging breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
- Repro window: intermittent capacity thrash and long tail cold starts for dedicated GPU pools (pools A/B/C) during peak traffic spikes (08:45-09:30 PST).
- Symptoms: repeated node add/remove churn, large number of warmup failures (~20% of new pods fail healthchecks), slow first-token latencies on new instances (20s+).
- Customer impact: increased p99 latency, brief errors (429/503) on heavy routes.

Observations / timeline (notes while investigating):
- 2026-02-18 08:46 - spike hit, autoscaler started launching nodes (g4-a1) in pool-A.
- 2026-02-18 08:50 - pool scale up to +6 nodes in ~4m, but then two nodes terminated within 2m of being ready.
- k8s events showed pod preStop hooks triggered, then node NotReady, then Drain started.
- Logs: "kubelet: failed to plug device plugin: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = device not found" on 2 nodes.
- We also saw model-server logs: "Failed to load model: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation" in ~8 warmup pods.

Commands tried / useful snippets:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels (look for taints/labels mismatch)
- kubectl describe node <node-id>  -- events: Node had taint controller.alpha.kubernetes.io/uninitialized:NoExecute (false-positive?)
- kubectl logs deploy/model-srv -c server --since=10m | grep -i cuda
- SSH to instance -> dmesg | tail -n 200 -> saw "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79" on one host (driver GPU fault).
- gcloud compute instances describe <instance> -> metadata shows preemptible:false, image: custom-inference-ubuntu-2026-01
- curl http://localhost:8080/health on new pods returned 500 for warmup function but 200 afterwards sometimes.
- ./scripts/scale-pool.sh --pool pool-A --count 0 -> forced scale down to zero locally to reproduce termination order.

Error snippets captured:
- "Failed to allocate device: resource busy" (kubelet/device-plugin)
- "cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory" (pytorch model load)
- dmesg: "NVRM: GPU at ... has fallen off the bus"
- k8s events: "Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created" repeated 3x

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Aggressive scale-down: cooldown too short (default 30s) causes nodes to be terminated before warmup completes -> results in thrash.
   - Evidence: scale-up then immediate scale-down in metrics, warmup pods killed <2m.
   - Test: increase scale-down cooldown to 5m for pool-A and monitor.
2) Prewarm container mismatch: warmup images/labels not matching admission webhook so prewarmed pods aren't reused by new workloads (label mismatch leads to fresh pods).
   - Evidence: newly launched pods have different nodeSelector label (gpu-type: g4-v1 vs g4-a1) in some cases.
   - Test: inspect admission webhook logs + nodeSelector injection logs.
3) GPU driver instability on certain host images -> GPU faults during init causing node to become NotReady and k8s to drain.
   - Evidence: dmesg NVRM Xid 79, device off the bus.
   - Test: repro with same image in staging, collect kernel/driver versions.
4) Device plugin race with kubelet startup ordering -> device plugin reports available GPUs but runtime not ready leading to "resource busy" errors.
   - Evidence: ordering in kubelet logs shows plugin init after CRI started.
   - Test: add init delay to plugin or coordinate systemd units.

Mitigations tried so far (quick wins):
- Increased scale-down cooldown from 30s -> 3m on pool-A (temporary). Observed immediate reduction in churn in next 24h window (good).
- Rolled back a recent kernel update on one suspicious image (custom-inference-ubuntu-2025-12 baseline) on 2 hosts; no NVRM Xid messages in subsequent 6h.
- Added more retries to warmup script (3 -> 6 retries with exponential backoff), decreased warmup timeout from 120s -> 90s to fail fast. Mixed results.
- Patch to device-plugin: log ordering + backoff before registering devices (PR linked).

Data to collect / logs to attach:
- kubelet logs (startup sequence) for nodes that terminated (node ids logged above) -> requested from infra team (Evan).
- full dmesg + nvidia-smi -q output at time of failure.
- autoscaler decision logs + metrics (scale events, CPU/GPU pressure) from 08:30-09:45 on incident days.
- model-server warmup logs + stack traces for OOM errors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there any recent changes to the node image or NVIDIA driver across pools? (Carlos to confirm).
- Is the admission webhook (that mutates prewarm pod labels) running at v1.3.2 or later? We saw a change in labels around 2026-01-12.
- Should we change the autoscaler policy: prefer scale-up margin + longer cooldown instead of aggressive scale-down?
- Can we add a prewarm "reserve" count in pool config (min_ready_gpu_containers) to ensure X warm pods always present?

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Evan: gather kubelet + autoscaler logs for nodes (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Carlos: confirm kernel/driver image rollouts and revert plan if needed (ETA: 2026-03-04).
- Priya: deploy cooldown config change to pool-A in staging, run load test, then prod if stable (ETA staging 2026-03-06).
- All: validate device-plugin PR in staging and coordinate rollout (TODO link PR in linked_artifacts).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc as breadcrumbs for incident postmortem. Capture exact node IDs + pod names when next thrash occurs.
- If we hit preemption behavior (cloud provider), include instance preempt logs.
- When repro locally, try to reproduce ordering: start device-plugin late, then launch model-server warmup.

Bottom line: immediate mitigation (longer cooldown) reduced visible churn; primary suspects are driver instability + race conditions in device plugin + aggressive scale-down policy. Need durable fixes: image pin/rollback, plugin ordering hardening, and autoscaler policy tweak.
